entities.name: Gaius Papirius Maso
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gaius Papirius Maso was a Roman consul of 231 BCE from the Papiria gens, active in the generation between the First and Second Punic Wars when Rome consolidated Italian hegemony and looked toward Cisalpine and overseas commitments. The Papirii Masones supplied several magistrates in the third century BCE.

His consulship belongs to the Fasti of a Republic professionalising warfare after Carthage’s first defeat. Such consuls managed Ligurian and Gallic frontiers while Rome’s attention drifted toward the Po valley and Illyria.

Maso is a Fasti marker of mid-Republican aristocratic continuity.
